paragraphs.source_en: While Ōtani Yoshitsugu was secretly making his way to Mount Matsuo to persuade Kobayakawa Hideaki, a small detachment sent to reconnoiter the enemy fled back to Ōgaki Castle in disarray at dusk. Ōgaki Castle was instantly thrown into chaos.

units.source_en: While Ōtani Yoshitsugu was secretly making his way to Mount Matsuo to persuade Kobayakawa Hideaki, a small detachment sent to reconnoiter the enemy fled back to Ōgaki Castle in disarray at dusk.
units.source_zh: 在大谷吉继悄悄赶赴松尾山，游说小早川秀秋的同时，薄暮中，一支去打探敌情的小分队狼狈逃回了大垣城。

units.source_en: Ōgaki Castle was instantly thrown into chaos.
units.source_zh: 大垣城内顿时乱作一团。

paragraphs.source_zh: 在大谷吉继悄悄赶赴松尾山，游说小早川秀秋的同时，薄暮中，一支去打探敌情的小分队狼狈逃回了大垣城。大垣城内顿时乱作一团。

paragraphs.source_en: The lord of Ōgaki Castle was Itō Morimasa. Ever since the Eastern Army commanders had begun encamping around Akasaka, he had feared that someone might collude with the enemy and foment disorder, so he detained the wealthy merchants from outside the castle as hostages within it. After news arrived that Ieyasu had come, these hostages grew even more alarmed than the warriors. Some even proposed that, since they were doomed to die anyway, they might as well set fire to the castle...

units.source_en: The lord of Ōgaki Castle was Itō Morimasa.
units.source_zh: 大垣城城主乃伊藤盛正。

units.source_en: Ever since the Eastern Army commanders had begun encamping around Akasaka, he had feared that someone might collude with the enemy and foment disorder, so he detained the wealthy merchants from outside the castle as hostages within it.
units.source_zh: 从东军诸将在赤坂一带安营扎寨时起，他因担心有人与敌人私通作乱，遂把城外大商家都扣到城里做了人质。

paragraphs.source_zh: 大垣城城主乃伊藤盛正。从东军诸将在赤坂一带安营扎寨时起，他因担心有人与敌人私通作乱，遂把城外大商家都扣到城里做了人质。在得知家康抵达的消息之后，这些人质比武士还要慌张。有人甚至提议，横竖是一死，干脆在城里放一把火……

paragraphs.source_en: Shima Sakon and Gamō Bitchū-no-kami, another senior retainer of the Ishida house, had joined forces and fought Nakamura of the Eastern Army, but could achieve no more than a draw, deepening the anxiety within the castle.

units.source_en: Shima Sakon and Gamō Bitchū-no-kami, another senior retainer of the Ishida house, had joined forces and fought Nakamura of the Eastern Army, but could achieve no more than a draw, deepening the anxiety within the castle.

paragraphs.source_en: “Before they left, they boasted that they would not return until they had annihilated the enemy. Yet here they are, back with heavy losses and their tails between their legs!”

units.source_en: “Before they left, they boasted that they would not return until they had annihilated the enemy. Yet here they are, back with heavy losses and their tails between their legs!”

He also said that Satake, Sanada, and the others had raised troops to attack him, so the Naifu could not possibly reach here. But from the looks of things now, the Naifu must be in command at Akasaka.”

units.source_zh: “我也觉得很是可疑。

paragraphs.source_en: Amid the clamor, Ukita Hideie and Konishi Yukinaga went in and out with bloodshot eyes, while the merchants' fear and confusion spread to the lower-ranking officers and soldiers.

paragraphs.source_en: In this atmosphere of confusion, after repeated deliberations, the Western Army finally decided to fight in the open field.

units.source_en: In this atmosphere of confusion, after repeated deliberations, the Western Army finally decided to fight in the open field.
units.source_zh: 在这样的混乱气氛中，经过反复磋商，西军最后决定进行野战。

paragraphs.source_en: In truth, even if the Western Army wished to defend the castle, victory would remain distant, for retreating behind its walls from the outset would be like a tiger entering a cage. Moreover, Kobayakawa Hideaki, encamped on Mount Matsuo, showed no sign at all of descending the mountain and entering the castle, while Natsuka Masaie and Ankokuji Ekei had both arrayed their forces south of Mount Nangū, plainly waiting to see which way the wind would blow.
